title: Free reading time is not instruction
statement: Don't rely on unguided independent reading time to raise reading outcomes, since a meta-analysis found that simply encouraging more independent reading did not improve them.
detail: The RAND Reading Study Group's 2002 report, in a reading course's digest of it, reports a National Reading Panel meta-analysis in which encouraging students to read more on their own, as in Sustained Silent Reading, did not result in improved reading (p. 32; `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`, lines 473-475). The same report notes that the panel found no compelling evidence that independent-reading programmes promoted vocabulary growth, while direct instruction of vocabulary did improve comprehension (p. 36). The vocabulary finding is an absence of evidence rather than a measured lack of effect.

evidence.quote: did not result in improved reading, according to the findings of a meta-analysis
A National Reading Panel meta-analysis found that simply encouraging students to read more independently (e.g., Sustained Silent Reading) did not improve reading outcomes.
The NRP did not find compelling evidence that programs that are designed to increase independent reading, such as Sustained Silent Reading, promoted vocabulary growth.
The NRP (2000) found that direct instruction of vocabulary improved reading comprehension.

citations.ref: RAND Reading Study Group 2002, Reading for Understanding (MR-1465)
